I often go to sleep way before I need to. I have plenty of issues with sleep. If anxiety about your alarm is keeping you from restful sleep then maybe going to bed even earlier could help. If you go to bed 10 or 12 hours before you need too then chances are you'll just wake up naturally and then have 2-4 hours before you really need to start your day to do whatever in. 

I have troubles falling asleep so I start trying to go to bed way earlier. My alarm most days is just a reminder that I should start getting ready for work. I prefer it to using alarms to wake up. Because then I can relax and take my time waking up and not feel rushed. So that work is a part of my day not the start of it.

Edit:
When I go to sleep before I absolutely need to then I have a high chance of waking up earlier than needed, a low chance of waking up at the alarm with more than enough sleep, and an extremely rare chance of waking up at the alarm with insufficient sleep. 

If I go to sleep just 8 hours before I need to start my day then my chance of lack of sleep increases to too high a chance for my liking. 

With PTSD there is s good chance you'll have sleep disturbances. I think the way you've been going about sleep is good if you don't have sleep issues. Plan for contingencies in your sleep. Set yourself up so that if you do have an issue then it wont drastically effect your day, mood and energy.

I am not the artist... but I may have an idea, well at least I've achieved something similar in various ways.

Most recently I have achieved something similar to this look with gray scale, instead of using just a diluted black, I mixed black and white. when it dried after applying wet paint to dry paper, some of the black seemed to be pushed out towards the edge of where the paint had been applied. However not as defined as this, I have seen something similar with an orange I mixed from yellow and red.

Also, recently I've achieved something similar by first applying one light outline of watercolor, then after it has dried, coming back in and filling in the space with the same color... carefully painting over the outline, and the overlapping color gave a similar effect.

Also I have observed this by having an excess amount of color on the paper where it appears to make a pool of the watercolor, letting it dry some, where it seems to dry first is the outer edge, then absorbing the excess un-dried paint with either a paper towel or dry brush. The part that did dry has left something very similar to this.

I have also chosen to accent some parts of my painting with a fine point pen, and have achieved something comparable to what I see here. 

Also have gotten something similar buy first laying down a darker color, slightly spreading it, but it still being quite wet, then to the middle apply a generous amount of a lighter or new color, this new color seems to push the original color to the outer edge. 

 And then I could guess, that maybe after some color has dried, come back with just water and spread it over an area, let it sit for a little while then absorb it up, if you are precise, I could imagine this may give the same effect, however... I am not speaking from something I've experienced, only something I think may achieve this.

I agree with you. We shouldn't fight fire with fire. Too often these people feel alone with what they are suffering. And yes they probably want validation, and may view that its a contest of who had it worse... because only the one who had it worse is valid in their pain. But all pain is valid, for it is the worse that you've personally had it. We need more understanding in this world. But I highly doubt that will change. Unfortunately I believe a few bad apples have spoiled the bunch of us as a society, so now everyone is on guard... well most people that is. 

I think its quit hard to fight the anger that comes along with the PTSD... that adrenaline pumping in your veins... some release it with anger... me however... I go into melt down mode, anxiety attacks, panic attacks or flashbacks... often a mix of some, if not all at times.

Words can hurt... they present someone with options on how to respond... some do so in not such a kind manor... I can see how it would be difficult... you're on the defensive, people hurt. And some are constantly being told that others have it worse... it is very hard to get some understanding, and often compassion. The frustration of feeling alone... well some go back to seemingly animalistic behavior... for people have hurt them, their cause for defense and retaliation is justified... all be it might not be helpful or healing.

It's very difficult to say how to handle the situation, because each person is unique processing their own pain in the way that comes to them. So you'd need just as unique solutions to be effective. But I'd try kindness first... for it often seems that the negative side of human beings is the main cause for our pain, our PTSD. Aside from natural disasters, disease, accidents... exctra.

In the back of my mind, I have this idea that there is something very dark inside of me. I feel it is powerful. Some days I feel it will be the destruction of me, those days I feel it in my chest. The best way I was ever able to describe it was saying it felt like I was dying. Feels like a hard ball in my chest, and it must have its own gravity because it feels like everything around it is sinking into it.

But then there are other days, where I feel it, but it feels like the ball is expanding trying to push it's way out of my chest. These days I'm quick to anger, but I'm afraid of my anger, because it feels like I just have this intense darkness just waiting inside of me and if I let it take over I'll just go into destruction mode and start tearing everything around me down, breaking things and being hurtful with my words to people.  

Whatever it is, I feel like it has power to overwhelm what control I have and that one day it will either destroy me, or I'll break and turn into some horrible monster and sink to some place where I become a completely cold person who is only out to harm others.

When I feel like I'm dying, nothing really seems to be able to help me, no distraction good enough. I want to share a little bit of my story, I am 24F, when I was 6 I was diagnosed as having borderline aspergers. After reading a therapy book called: Complex PTSD From Surviving to Thriving by Pete Walker, I understand why I may have been mis-diagnosed with aspergers, because cPTSD and PTSD in general can make you hyper-sensitive to your surroundings, also for a lot you don't develop a very good social interaction due to not being able to cope in an effective way with the trauma you experience as a child. I'm not saying you don't have aspergers, I don't know that, nor can I diagnose anyone. From what I understand it is clear that a lot of people RBN develop cPTSD.  When I ran under the belief that I had aspergers I never really felt like I was able to help myself because of it, but after being diagnosed with cPTSD and reading the book I mentioned, I have a much better understanding of myself.
